# Results — Study 535 (Mispricing-Score) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: a Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan (2015)
**composite mispricing score** — the average of six price-computable anomaly ranks (12-1 momentum,
MAX/lottery, 6-month volatility, 12-month price run-up, distance to the 52-week high, short-term
reversal), each oriented so HIGH = more overpriced. Monthly, LONG the cheapest quintile and SHORT
the most-overpriced quintile, equal-weight, one-day execution lag, on a large-cap S&P 500 survivor
panel. As-of **2026-06-27**.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Edge in the short leg?" `BUSTED`

Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan (2015) say a composite of eleven anomalies sorts the cross-section better than
any single one, and that the predictive power lives in the **short (overpriced) leg**. On a
45-name large-cap survivor basket the composite **does sort** — a label-shuffle placebo puts the
realised spread far in the tail (**p = 0.007**) — but it sorts the **wrong way**: the long-short
**loses −7.68%/yr gross** (HAC *t* = −1.84), **−9.50%/yr net** of costs (HAC *t* = −2.28). The
"overpriced" short leg returned **+23.1%/yr** — the *best* basket to own, not short — because on a
survivor universe the high-momentum, high-vol, near-52-week-high names are exactly the mega-cap
winners (the NVDA/AAPL cohort) that kept winning, and the failed overpriced names that would have
made the SYY short leg pay have been **deleted from the sample**. The synthetic positive control
confirms the engine is faithful (it recovers a planted premium monotonically and prints ~0 at the
null), so the adverse result is **the survivor tape**, not the method. `NONE` signal (no positive
*t* ≥ 2; the only significance is against the strategy), `MIRAGE` tradability (loses gross and net,
−80% drawdown), short-leg edge `BUSTED` on survivors.

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 4023 days × 45 tickers | `b6d4a14d508b` |
| SPY (context series) | 4023 days | `5bb6e49fae4d` |
| Period covered | 2010-01-04 — 2025-12-30 | — |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True). Universe: 45 large-cap S&P 500
names. The panel is **survivorship-biased** — current members projected backwards.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** only companies that survived to 2026 are in the sample.
The worst overpriced names — natural short candidates and the engine of SYY's short-leg edge — have
delisted and are absent. This biases the short leg's apparent return **upward** and is the direct
cause of the adverse long-short result. All numbers are upper-bound *on the long leg* and a
best-case (least-adverse) bound on the short leg.

## The composite long-short — it sorts, adversely

Six anomaly signals → cross-sectional percentile ranks → averaged into one score → quintile sort.
LONG cheapest quintile, SHORT most-overpriced quintile, equal-weight, one-day execution lag.

| Statistic | Gross | Net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|
| N months | 178 (2011-02 — 2025-11) | 178 |
| Mean return (annualised) | **−7.68%/yr** | **−9.50%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 16.25%/yr | 16.3%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | −0.473 | −0.585 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **−1.843** | **−2.285** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 43.3% | — |
| Max drawdown | −80.3% | — |
| Avg monthly turnover | 44.8% | — |

Costs: 10 bps/side × turnover × 2 legs + 75 bps/yr borrow on the short leg. Net is **more** negative
than gross — costs deepen the loss; there is no positive edge for them to erode.

## Where is the edge? (SYY say the short leg — on survivors it's the opposite)

| Leg | Mean return | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| Long (cheapest quintile) | **+15.45%/yr** | **+4.26** |
| "Overpriced" names (raw, owned) | +23.13%/yr | — |
| Short BOOK (shorting the overpriced names) | **−23.13%/yr** | **−5.04** |

The long (cheap) leg is a clean, significant **long-only defensive tilt** — the only salvageable
piece. The short leg is a catastrophe: on survivors, the "overpriced" glamour names are the
decade's biggest winners, so shorting them bleeds −23%/yr.

## Placebo — the score genuinely sorts (just adversely)

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Observed long-short mean | −7.68%/yr |
| Null mean (150 label-shuffles) | −0.13%/yr |
| Null std | 3.05%/yr |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.007** |

A random permutation of the composite score across names destroys the spread (null ≈ 0). The
observed −7.68% sits far in the tail (p = 0.007): the ranking carries **real cross-sectional
information**. It is just pointed the wrong way for a long-short on this survivor universe.

## Robustness — sharper cutoffs deepen the loss (monotone, not a fluke)

| Tail cutoff | Long-short mean | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| Tercile (top/bottom 30%) | −4.69%/yr | −1.49 |
| Quintile (top/bottom 20%) | −7.68%/yr | −1.84 |
| Decile (top/bottom 10%) | −11.66%/yr | −2.08 |

The more extreme the "overpriced" tail, the worse the short leg — the loss is structural, not a
single-cutoff artefact.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Plant a mispricing premium (overpriced = high-vol names that then underperform) and sweep it;
the composite long-short mean should be monotone in the premium and ≈ 0 at the null. Averaged over
15 seeds (Welch-style):

| Planted premium | L-S mean (15 seeds) |
|---|--:|
| −0.20 | −5.84%/yr |
| −0.10 | −2.11%/yr |
| 0.00 | **−0.03%/yr** (null ≈ 0) |
| +0.10 | +2.73%/yr |
| +0.20 | +4.42%/yr |
| +0.30 | +4.33%/yr |

Monotone and zero at the null: the engine detects a planted mispricing premium when one exists.
The real-tape failure therefore reflects the **survivor market**, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The composite *sorts* (placebo p = 0.007), but the long-short as SYY specify
  it earns **no positive** *t* ≥ 2 — the only significant *t* is **negative** (−1.84 gross, −2.28
  net). There is no real *positive* edge on this tape. Literature support (SYY 2012/2015) cannot
  upgrade a wrong-signed, insignificant-in-the-intended-direction result; per the house bar that is
  NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Loses gross (−7.68%/yr) and net (−9.50%/yr), Sharpe −0.47, max drawdown
  −80%. Costs deepen the loss. Untradeable as a long-short.
- **"Edge in the short leg?" — BUSTED.** SYY's headline is that the short (overpriced) leg drives
  the spread. On survivors the short leg is the single worst place to be: shorting the "overpriced"
  names loses −23%/yr (*t* = −5.04), because the failed overpriced names that would make it pay have
  delisted. The only honest, tradable residue is the **long (cheap) leg as a long-only tilt**
  (+15.45%/yr, *t* +4.26) — and even that is dominated by the survivor mega-cap rally, not by
  cheapness.
